The Bisra Stone Lime Company Limited (BSLC) | footnotes = | intl = | hq_location_country = [[India]] | website = {{URL|www.vizagsteel.com}} }} '''Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd''' (abbreviated as '''RINL'''), also known as ''Vizag Steel'', is a [[Public sector undertakings in India|central public sector undertaking]] under the [[ownership]] of [[Ministry of Steel]], [[Government of India]] based in [[Visakhapatnam]], [[India]]. Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL) is the government entity of '''Visakhapatnam Steel Plant''' (VSP), India's first shore-based integrated steel plant built with state-of-the-art technology. Visakhapatnam Steel Plant (VSP) is a 7.3 MTPA plant. It was commissioned in 1992 with a capacity of 3.0 MTPA of liquid steel. The CPSU subsequently completed its capacity expansion to 6.3 MTPA in April 2015 and to 7.3 MTPA in December 2017. The PSU is having one [[subsidiary]], viz. Eastern Investment Limited (EIL) with 51% shareholding, which in turn is having two [[Subsidiary|subsidiaries]], viz. M/s Orissa Mineral Development Company Ltd (OMDC) and M/s Bisra Stone Lime Company Ltd (BSLC). The CPSU has a partnership in RINMOIL Ferro Alloys Private Limited and International Coal Ventures Limited in the form of Joint Ventures with 50% and 26.49% shareholding respectively. RINL is wholly owned by the [[Government of India]]. ==Location== The steel plant is in the southern part of [[Visakhapatnam]] city, Andhra Pradesh state of India. The company has blast furnace grade Limestone captive mine at Jaggayyapeta (Krishna District), a captive mine for Dolomite at Madharam (Khammam), a manganese ore captive mine at Cheepurupalli (Vizianagaram). It also has a mining lease for river sand on the [[river Champavathi]]. ==History== [[File:Pylon at Vizag Steel Plant 01.jpg|right|thumb|250px|Pylon at Vizag Steel Plant]] [[File:Vizag Steel.jpg|right|thumb|Vizag Steel]] On 17 April 1970, the Prime Minister of India, [[Indira Gandhi]], announced the government's decision to establish a steel plant at Visakhapatnam. With the offer of assistance from the government of the erstwhile [[USSR]], a revised project evolved some years later. A detailed project report for a plant with a capacity of 3.4 Mtpa was prepared in November 1980 and in February 1981, a contract was signed with the USSR for the preparation of working drawings of [[coke ovens]], [[blast furnace]] and [[sinter plant]]. The blast furnace foundation was laid, with first mass concreting, in January 1982. The construction of the local township was also started at the same time.{{cite web|title=A supreme sacrifice that brought VSP to Vizag|url=http://www.thehansindia.com/posts/index/Andhra-Pradesh/2016-11-01/A-supreme-sacrifice-that-brought-VSP-to-Vizag/261901|website=The Hans India|date=November 2016 |access-date=23 April 2018}} In the 1970s, Kurupam Zamindars donated 6,000 acres of land for Vizag Steel Plant. A new company [[Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited]] (RINL) was formed on 18 February 1982. Visakhapatnam Steel Plant was separated from [[Steel Authority of India Limited|SAIL]] and RINL was made the corporate entity of Visakhapatnam Steel Plant in April 1982.{{cite web|title=Vizag Steel Plant in Visakhapatnam|url=http://www.visakhapatnamonline.in/city-guide/vizag-steel-plant-in-visakhapatnam|website=Visakhapatanam Online|publisher=India Online|access-date=23 April 2018}} Vizag Steel Plant is the only Indian shore-based steel plant and is situated on {{convert|33000|acre}}, and is poised to expand to produce up to 20 MT in a single campus. Turnover in 2011-2012 was Rs 14,457 [[crores]]. On 20 May 2009, Prime Minister [[Manmohan Singh]] launched the expansion project of Visakhapatnam Steel Plant from a capacity of 3.6 MT to 6.3 MT at a cost of Rs. 8,692 crores. But the investment was revised to 14,489 crores with the following classification: * Expenditure for the financial year 2009-10 Rs 1840 crores. * Rs 5883 crores since inception of the project. * Total commitment, including enabling works, steel procurement, consultancy, spares, etc. is Rs 11591 crores as of 25 March 2010. In November 2010, the company was granted the ''Navratna'' status by the Government of India.{{cite web|url=http://www.vizagsteel.com/code/press/pressrelfiles/34116.11.10-navratna.pdf|title=RINL conferred ''Navratna'' status|publisher=Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited|date=16 November 2010|access-date=2 September 2011}}{{cite news| url= http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/article3509492.ece| title=Visakhapatnam Steel Plant unions serve strike notice | date=10 June 2012}} In September 2011, the government announced plans to divest 10% of its stake in RINL via an [[initial public offering]]. In February 2021, the Cabinet approved the privatisation of steel-maker Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd (RINL). capacity steel plant in [[Visakhapatnam]].{{cite web|url=http://www.vizagsteel.com/index.asp?sm=1&url=code/Infrastr/ccp.asp|title=Expansion Plans|publisher=Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited|access-date=2 September 2011}} The '''Visakhapatnam Steel Plant''' is the integrated steel plant founded in 1982 that focuses on producing value-added steel, producing 5.773 million tonnes of hot metal, 5.272 million tonnes of crude steel and 5.138 million tonnes of saleable steel in the 2021-2022 financial year.{{cite news |date=2 April 2022 |title=Splendid performance by Visakhapatnam Steel Plant in 2021-22 |work=[[New Indian Express]] |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/andhra-pradesh/2022/apr/02/splendid-performance-by-visakhapatnam-steel-plant-in-2021-22-2437056.html |access-date=10 June 2022}} According to the India Daily Times, the plant is expected to skyrocket in terms of production in the nearest future. During the initial periods, the company suffered huge losses. Later the profits have gone up by 200% making it the only steel industry to achieve such a target. Its annual capacity is expected to reach almost 7.5 million tonnes by 2020. RINL plans to invest {{INRConvert|60000|c}} to increase the capacity to 20 million tonnes by 2027.{{Cite news|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/rinl-to-invest-rs-60k-cr-to-have-20-mt-capacity-by-2027-113100300764_1.html|title=RINL to invest Rs 60K cr to have 20 MT capacity by 2027|agency=Press Trust of India|date=2013-10-03|newspaper=Business Standard|access-date=2016-10-23}} ===Safety incidents === *On 13 June 2012, 19 people died during a trial run of recently http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/hyderabad/Massive-explosion-and-fire-in-Vizag-Steel-plant-16-dead-many-injured/articleshow/14102942.cms| title=Massive explosion and fire in Vizag Steel plant, 16 dead, many injured | date=13 June 2012}} Union Steel Minister Beni Prasad Verma visited and announced {{INRConvert|20|l}} [[Ex gratia]] to each person. * In June 2014, two engineers were fatally injured in a suspected case of [[Carbon monoxide poisoning]].{{cite news|title=Two engineers killed in accident at Vizag Steel Plant|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/news-ians/two-engineers-killed-in-accident-at-vizag-steel-plant-114061600984_1.html|work=[[Business Standard]]|date=16 June 2014}} *On 7 November 2014, a minor explosion occurred in the Blast Furnace II but there were no casualties.{{cite news|title=Minor explosion in Vizag Steel Plant blast furnace|url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Visakhapatnam/minor-explosion-in-vizag-steel-plant-blast-furnace/article6574461.ece|work=[[The Hindu]]|date=7 Nov 2014}} *In February 2015, an assistant general manager was involved in a fatal incident when he fell into a rotating drum.{{cite news|last1=Patnaik|first1=Santosh|title=Vizag Steel Plant official dies in industrial mishap|url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Visakhapatnam/vsp-official-dies-in-freak-mishap/article6887540.ece|work=[[The Hindu]]|date=12 Feb 2015}} *On 18 January 2019, a hot metal pipe was exploded in Blast furnace number 3. There were no casualties.{{cite news|title=Explosion in Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, none injured| url= https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Visakhapatnam/explosion-in-visakhapatnam-steel-plant-none-injured/article26024446.ece|work=[[The Hindu]]|date=18 January 2019}} *On 9 June 2026, an explosion occurred in a ladle carrying molten steel at the steel melting shop . The blast triggered a fire and spilled hundreds of tonnes of molten steel, killing eight workers and injuring six others. Five regular employees and three contract workers were reported among the fatalities.{{Cite web |date=2026-06-08 |title=First a blast, then molten steel at 1,500°C falls to floor: What we know about Vizag Steel Plant accident |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/india/vizag-steel-plant-blast-rinl-visakhapatnam-accident-deaths-investigation-10730294/ |access-date=2026-06-09 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}} ==Township== The Visakhapatnam Steel Plant Township (VSPT), also known as '''Ukkunagaram''' ({{lit|Steel City}}) was developed on 8000 acres of land, providing housing and accommodations for many of the employees. The township has 8200 dwellings spread over 12 sectors and 3900 acres, as well as a green belt of 4260 acres. The town also has multiple temples, churches, a mosque, gurudwara, athletic facilities, hospital, police station, post office, shopping malls, schools, indoor and outdoor stadiums. Some of the most famous temples include the Shivalayam, Goddess Kali temple, Venkateshwara temple, Shirdi Baba temple, Puri Jagannadh temple, Tri-Shakti temple, Ayyapa temple, and the Sathya Sai Baba Mandir.{{citation needed|date=January 2019}} Besides, there are marriage halls and clubs{{citation needed|date=January 2019}} for conducting various activities for entertainment such as screening of movies, hosting parties, felicitating people and celebrating festivals. ==References== {{Reflist|30em}} ==External links== {{commons category|Visakhapatnam Steel Plant}} * {{Official website|http://www.vizagsteel.com/}} {{Steel industry of India}} {{Public Sector Undertakings in India}} {{Visakhapatnam}} {{authority control}} [[Category:Steel companies of India]] [[Category:Companies based in Visakhapatnam]] [[Category:Manufacturing companies established in 1982]] [[Category:Economy of Visakhapatnam]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 1982]] [[Category:Recipients of the Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puruskar]]
